name: Chez Panisse
notes: Alice Waters' restaurant, widely credited as the origin of the modern California farm-to-table movement — daily-changing menu built around local, seasonal produce.

name: Blue Hill at Stone Barns
notes: Chef Dan Barber's restaurant sits on a working farm; the menu is built directly from what the farm is producing that week.

name: The Herbfarm
notes: Long-running Pacific Northwest restaurant built around its own herb gardens and regional foraged/farmed ingredients.

name: Husk
notes: Chef Sean Brock's Southern restaurant, sourced almost entirely from Southern farms, mills, and producers.

name: Canlis
notes: Iconic Seattle restaurant known for close relationships with regional Pacific Northwest farms and fisheries.

name: The Publican
notes: Nose-to-tail, beer-and-oyster-focused restaurant with a strong emphasis on responsibly raised meat and produce.

name: Girl & the Goat
notes: Stephanie Izard's restaurant, known for shareable, produce- and farm-forward small plates.

name: Zingerman's Roadhouse
notes: Part of the Zingerman's family of businesses, built around American regional cooking with named small-farm sourcing.

name: Vinegar Hill House
notes: Seasonal, market-driven menu in a small Brooklyn neighborhood restaurant.

name: The Grey
notes: Southern restaurant in a restored 1938 Greyhound bus terminal, sourced from regional Lowcountry farms and fisheries.

name: Nopa
notes: Wood-fired, organic-leaning neighborhood restaurant, open late, longtime SF favorite.

name: True Food Kitchen
notes: National chain built around an anti-inflammatory, whole-food philosophy — quality/sourcing can vary by location, as with any multi-city chain.

name: Local Ocean Seafood
notes: Restaurant and fish market on the Oregon coast built around day-boat, locally landed seafood.

name: Eleven Madison Park
notes: Since 2021, an entirely plant-based fine-dining menu built around regional farm sourcing — a notable, widely covered shift for a restaurant of its stature.

name: Steak 'n Shake
notes: In 2024, publicly announced switching to 100% beef tallow for its fries — a widely reported, real change, not a general claim about every menu item. Verify current practice at a given location before relying on it for a dietary need.
